title: Terraform Upgrade Assistant: staged-safe-upgrades, preflight drift detection, OPA policy gate
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: Upgrading Terraform modules and provider versions across customer VPC deployments is risky: state drift, non-idempotent changes, and silent failures have caused incident work and rollback churn. Goal: Implement a reusable pipeline and small orchestration helper (Upgrade Assistant) that performs preflight checks, policy gates (OPA/Conftest), staged canary apply, automated health checks, and safe rollback snapshots as part of our IaC CI/CD for Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable pipeline template (GitHub Actions + runner pool) exists that runs lint -> plan -> policy-eval -> staged-apply -> verify
Preflight: terraform plan runs produce deterministic plan files and are stored as immutable artifacts for audit
Policy-as-code enforcement: OPA/Conftest checks block non-compliant plans with clear failure messages
Canary apply: the pipeline can apply changes to an isolated canary workspace (customer sandbox or small subset of infra) and run health probes before progressing
State backup: remote state snapshots are taken to object storage with encryption before any apply and are restorable by automation
Rollback: automated rollback runner can restore state snapshot and re-apply previous plan within 15 minutes of a failed verification
Metrics & alerts: per-upgrade dashboard with plan/apply success, drift-rate, and a PagerDuty/Slack trigger when verification fails
Documentation: runbook, SRE playbook, and template PR for customers/solutions engineers are published
implementation_plan: Create a reusable GitHub Actions workflow (or next-gen runner) that performs the following stages: tf-lint (tflint/tfsec/checkov), fmt-check, terraform init + validate, terraform plan -out, upload plan artifact
Build a policy-evaluator step: run Conftest with OPA policies compiled to WASM for fast/easy sandbox execution; fail pipeline on deny with human-readable diagnostics
Implement plan-signing: store plan metadata and checksum in artifact store and attach to PR for auditability
Add a canary workspace template: small, representative state with minimum resources and mocked external integrations for fast verification
Canary apply runner: apply plan in canary workspace, run post-apply healthchecks (API ping, connectivity tests, internal app smoke tests) using the same probes as runtime monitoring
Staged rollout orchestration: if canary passes, allow automated or gated promotion to broader environments in waves (50%, 100%), controlled by policy and release flags
State snapshot & retention: before each apply, export remote state encrypted to object store (S3/GCS) and tag with pipeline run id; provide a restore helper utility
Rollback automation: implement a restore job that can rehydrate state from snapshot and re-apply last-known-good plan; include dry-run option
Telemetry: emit metrics (plan_duration_seconds, apply_success, verification_status) to observability and wire into a dashboard and alert rules
Access controls: ensure KMS keys and service accounts used for state snapshot/restore are auditable and require least privilege
testing_plan: Unit: policy rules exercised with Conftest unit cases for common deny scenarios
Integration: run pipeline against a test cluster with synthetic customer module revisions (use terratest or kitchen-terraform)
Chaos: introduce drift into canary workspace to validate detection and rollback behavior
Performance: validate plan artifact upload/download and policy-eval times to keep pipeline under SLA (target median <= 2 minutes for policy-eval)
Security: secrets and state snapshot encryption verified in a pen-test checklist
rollback_strategy: Immediate: if post-apply verification fails, pipeline triggers state-restore job referencing the prior snapshot and re-applies prior plan
Fallback: if automated restore fails, open an incident channel, provide a manual restore playbook, and escalate to on-call infra
Verification: after restore, run the same acceptance health probes and only close the incident when all green
Retention: keep last 5 snapshots per workspace for quick restores and forensic analysis
notes: Tradeoffs: full automatic promotion reduces manual toil but increases blast radius; will gate production promotion behind an approval step for high-risk customers
Design: prefer Conftest/OPA with WASM to allow running policies in multiple CI runners and eventually embed policy checks in the runtime preflight hook
Consideration: support for Terragrunt wrapper required for some customer repos; pipeline template will include optional terragrunt mode
Edge cases: state schema changes (resource rename) may still need manual intervention; add detection to surface potentially destructive diffs early
Ops: implement a dry-run toggle so SREs can rehearse restores without touching live state
